How phase and bars ago are set

Phase = the Wyckoff phase of the ticker's own daily range on the Wyckoff Structure page when that range is an accumulation / re-accumulation (19 of 187 rows). Everything else is No range · trending: no Structure range at all, or a distribution range (24 rows, noted under the ticker). No Phase-E guess is made without a range: a Minervini base in a Trend Template uptrend is a trend, not a trading range. Bars ago = sessions since the trigger / breakout bar when the setup has one, otherwise since it was first flagged (start of its current unbroken run in the daily detection log, feeds/setups/detections_log.jsonl).

Method (locked rules): SEPA = Minervini's Specific Entry Point Analysis. SETUP (as of the session before the trigger): S1 Trend Template passes (all 6); S2 RS ≥80; S3 close within 15% of the 52-week high; S4 base from the highest high 15–130 sessions back, depth ≤35%; S5 ≥2 pullbacks (5% zigzag), last shallower than first and ≤12%; S6 last 10 sessions' range ≤10% of the close; S7 10-day avg volume < 50-day; S8 pivot = highest high of the final contraction, structure stop = 1% under its low, risk ≤8% (else 'setup, risk too wide'); S9 RS-universe liquidity. BUY on a session T in the last 3: B1 close above the pivot; B2 volume ≥1.5× 50-day; B3 close in the upper half of the day's range; B4 close ≤5% above the pivot; B5 open ≤3% above the pivot; B6 entry risk to the structure stop ≤8%; B7 market pulse not defensive; B8 no known earnings on T or the next 5 sessions (unknown = 'earnings unchecked', never a pass). Still a buy only while today's close is between the pivot and +5%. Failed breakout = close under the stop, or back under the pivot within 3 sessions. Statuses: buy · extended, no buy · breakout, low volume, no buy · gap, no buy · weak close, no buy · risk too wide · market defensive, no buy · setup, earnings pending · failed breakout · intraday break, no close above pivot · setup, risk too wide · setup, within 5% of pivot · setup. Method: Prior uptrend (base top ≥30% above the 126-session low before it, or ≥25% over the 200-day at base start; close > 200-day now). Base = highest high 15–65 sessions back (right side ≤5% above it). Pullbacks from a 5% high/low zigzag (lower lows merged): 2–4, each shallower, first 10–40%. Volume: last pullback's avg < first's and 10-day avg < 50-day. Tight: final 5 sessions' range ≤8%. Coiling = close within 5% below the pivot (highest high since the last pullback began). Triggered = close above the pivot on >1.5× 50-day volume in the last 3 sessions, still above it. Stop = 1% under the final 5-session low.

Method: Stage 1: ≥100% close-to-close gain within the 40 sessions (8 weeks) ending at the peak close, 15–75 sessions ago. Stage 2 base: lowest close ≤25% below the peak, no close under the 50-day, 15–75 sessions (3–15 weeks), average volume below the advance's. Pivot = highest high since the peak. Breakout = close above it on ≥1.4× 50-day volume in the last 3 sessions, still above; else base forming. Stop = 1% under the base's last 5-session low.

Method: Run: ≥100% close-to-close within the 40 sessions ending at the peak close. Flag: 15–25 sessions (3–5 weeks) since the peak, high-low depth ≤20%, average volume ≤0.75× the run's and 10-day < 50-day. Pivot = flag high. Breakout = close above it on ≥1.4× 50-day volume in the last 3 sessions; else flag forming. Stop = 1% under the last 5-session low. Overlap: an HTF is an early, tighter power play; names meeting both are cross-labelled.

Method: Trend Template pass + ≥20% advance into the base. Base = longest window of 25–65 sessions (5–13 weeks) with total depth ≤15%, average daily range 1–5%, and lower volume in its second half. Base forming = close within 5% below the pivot (base high). Breakout = close above it on ≥1.4× 50-day volume in the last 3 sessions. Stop = 1% under the last 5-session low.

How phase and bars ago are set

Phase comes from the Wyckoff Structure page when the same ticker + timeframe has an accumulation range containing the spring (34 springs), otherwise from the spring's own events (686): forming / confirmed / test = Phase C, SOS or breakout = Phase D, ≥ ½ range height above the top = Phase E, failed / breakdown = its own group. A spring is a Phase C event; Phase D/E means it has already been followed by an SOS / LPS or markup. Bars ago = bars since the spring bar in its own timeframe (D sessions · W weeks · M months). TR = trading-range spring · Uptrend = shakeout in an uptrend.

Trading-range spring method: Wyckoff trading-range spring (accumulation, Phase C), daily / weekly / monthly. Context: a prior decline (the highest high of the 120 daily bars before the selling climax is >= 20% above it, or >= 12% with a wide-range, high-volume down bar; weekly 30%, monthly 40%). Range: support = the SC/ST lows, resistance (creek) = the automatic-rally high; >= 20 daily bars (8 weeks, 6 months), 8-60% high (daily), an ST back in the bottom 25% of the range, no markup above the AR. Spring: a low under support with a close back above it within 5 daily bars (3 weeks, 2 months); penetration <= 15% / 3 ATR / half the range (deeper = breakdown). Shallow <= 0.5 ATR and <= 3% (daily); shakeout >= 1.25 ATR or >= 5%. Pruden: #3 shallow + light volume (<= 1x the 50-bar average), #1 deep + heavy volume (>= 1.5x) = terminal shakeout, #2 the rest. Statuses: spring forming (fresh break showing demand, not reclaimed) / spring confirmed / test in progress / SOS breakout (close above the creek) / failed (a close below the spring low). Score 0-100 = speed + extent of the recovery + volume on the break + test + follow-through + context. Actionable: #3 reclaimed in the last few bars, #1/#2 only after a low-volume test lifts off, or a fresh SOS on volume; risk to the stop 1% under the spring low within the per-timeframe cap. Trade plan (desk rule): entry = buy stop 0.1% above the spring-bar high, live from the bar after the spring bar (a gap above it fills at the open), status triggered once traded; stop 1% under the spring low; the creek / range top is shown as a level, not the entry. VSA context (vsa.py) is shown alongside but never changes a spring. Rules: research-tools/springs_config.json, sources: research-tools/SPRINGS_METHOD.md.

Uptrend spring method: Uptrend (re-accumulation) spring: stock in an established uptrend (close > rising 200-day, 150 > 200, >= 25% advance into the range, range top within 15% of the 52-week high; RS >= 70) builds a 15-80-session range (6-35% deep); price then undercuts the range low (daily: or the last higher pivot low, Minervini's undercut & rally) and closes back above it within 4 sessions. Shallow <= 0.5 ATR / 3%; deep shakeout >= 1.25 ATR or 5%. Pruden #3 = shallow on light volume (<= 1x), #1 = deep on heavy volume (>= 1.5x, a shakeout that must be absorbed/tested), #2 = between. Score = reclaim speed 25 + recovery toward the range high 20 + volume signature 20 + low-volume test 15 + tightening/breakout 20. Stop 1% under the spring-bar low, trailed under recent lows. Weekly/monthly use the same rules on resampled bars (weekly MAs 10/30/40, monthly 3/7/10).

Near-misses (broke a range low but failed one rule; highest RS first): MXL D undercut too small (0.53%, 0.05 ATR) · AXTI W range check failed: width_pct · CLYM D range check failed: width_pct · ERAS D range check failed: width_atr · ANRO D range check failed: prior_decline · CUE D range check failed: width_pct · LIFE D range check failed: prior_decline · LIND D range check failed: prior_decline · OKTA D range check failed: prior_decline · STX D undercut too small (0.45%, 0.06 ATR) · DFTX D range check failed: prior_decline · ICHR D range check failed: width_pct · PRAX D weak spring score 36 < 40 · RLAY D range check failed: prior_decline · BB D undercut too small (0.52%, 0.08 ATR) · ZBRA D context at range start: mid_gt_slow · IBRX D context at range start: near_high · IOSP D range depth 3.4% outside 6-35% · MU D range depth 41.2% outside 6-35% · DE D range depth 5.7% outside 6-35% · EXPD D range depth 4.2% outside 6-35% · PM D RS 64 < 70 · FIVN D context at range start: mid_gt_slow · IMOS D range depth 44.5% outside 6-35% · CVBF D RS 61 < 70 · OMER D penetration 95% of the range height (too deep for a spring) · EQIX D RS 69 < 70 · NWSA D RS 60 < 70 · HAFC D RS 65 < 70 · LILAK D context at range start: mid_gt_slow

📈 Springs track record → point-in-time replay of both detectors (forward 5/10/20-day results, +2R before stop, rule studies).

TF = timeframe (D daily, W weekly, M monthly; the newest week/month may still be open). Type: TR = trading-range (accumulation after a decline), Uptrend = re-accumulation spring. Depth: shallow / moderate / shakeout. Pruden #3 = minor penetration on light volume vs the average AND vs the range's own earlier down-swings (best, no test needed; Pruden: very rare); #2 = needs a test; #1 = terminal shakeout on heavy volume, reclaimed - needs a successful test; breakdown #1 = not reclaimed, rally stalled at old support on ~half the breakdown volume: never a buy (short-side warning). Actionable also needs P&F reward/risk ≥ 3 (conservative count target). Weis depth = (rally high − spring low) ÷ (rally high − support); above 1.5 Weis would not call it a spring. Weis path = heavy-volume break, next bar narrower with no lower close, support reclaimed (he buys before the test). Both are information only, not gates. Vol on break = heaviest bar from the break to the spring low ÷ its average (≤1× light, ≥1.5× heavy). Score 0–100 = recovery speed + extent + volume + test + follow-through + context; rec = recovery-only score. VSA context comes from vsa.py and never creates, drops or reclassifies a spring. Rules: research-tools/springs_config.json · sources: research-tools/SPRINGS_METHOD.md.

Returns from the touch-bar close. Stop-aware = exit at the setup stop (or the open if it gapped below) when hit within 20 sessions, else the +20 close.

Confirmed buy signal: VCP 'triggered' (setup_vcp.py): all six VCP rules hold as of the session before (prior uptrend, 3-13 week base, 2-4 successively shallower pullbacks, first 10-40%, volume dry-up, final 5-session range <= 8%, close within 5% of the pivot), then a close above the pivot on > 1.5x the 50-day average volume. Stop = 1% under the final 5-session low. Power Play 'breakout' (setup_powerplay.py): >= 100% gain in 8 weeks to a peak 3-15 weeks ago, then a base <= 25% deep that holds the 50-day on lighter volume, then a close above the pivot (highest high since the peak) on >= 1.4x 50-day volume. Stop = 1% under the base's last 5-session low. SEPA 'buy' (setup_sepa.py): setup rules S1-S8 on the prior session and all buy rules B1-B8 on the trigger session (close > pivot, volume >= 1.5x 50-day, upper-half close, close <= pivot+5%, open <= pivot+3%, risk <= 8%, market not defensive, no known earnings within 5 sessions). Structure stop = 1% under the final contraction's low.

Touch: First touch = the first daily bar after the signal bar whose low is at or below the upper edge of the zone between EMA10 and EMA20 of daily closes (alpha 2/(n+1)) as they stood going into that session (through the prior close) - the same as price meeting the live EMA line intraday. Only that first touch is flagged; the signal is then closed for good. A signal also closes if its stop is hit first (bar low <= stop; when the stop sits above the zone price must cross it first) or after 40 sessions without a touch. Intraday (hourly alerts): Yahoo's live low vs the prior-day EMA zone (approximate), finalised by the next daily run.

Backfill: signals before 25 Sep 2026 come from setup_backfill.py as-of scans (origin 'backfill') and are replayed bar by bar; survivorship (delisted names absent). Small sample - not a statistically robust edge. Intraday alerts compare Yahoo's live low with the prior-day EMA zone (approximate); the daily run finalises the touch on the RS-cache closing bar (Massive grouped-daily, split-adjusted). Forward returns are from the touch-bar close, close-to-close, no costs; windows overlap. Source: feeds/ema_pullback/latest.json (research-tools/ema_pullback.py).

ℹ️ How the earnings score works

0–100, in the spirit of Minervini / CANSLIM: big and accelerating earnings and sales. Each component scores 0–1 by straight-line interpolation between the points shown (value → score; growth in %, margin in percentage points), then is weighted. Growth is capped at +300%. A loss-to-profit quarter is a turnaround (“TA”, scores 0.8) instead of an infinite %. Missing components are dropped and the remaining weights re-normalised; below 60% coverage, fewer than 5 quarters of EPS, or a latest quarter older than 200 days the name is tagged Limited data (score shown with “~”, kept out of the Top lists).

ComponentWeightPoints (value→score)
Latest-quarter EPS growth YoY250→0 · 25→0.45 · 50→0.7 · 100→1
EPS acceleration (last 3 quarters' YoY growth rising)15
Latest-quarter sales growth YoY150→0 · 10→0.35 · 25→0.7 · 50→1
Sales acceleration (last 3 quarters)5
3-year annual EPS growth (CAGR)100→0 · 15→0.5 · 25→0.8 · 40→1
Forward EPS growth (consensus: next FY vs this FY 55%, this FY vs last 45%)150→0 · 15→0.5 · 25→0.75 · 50→1
Last EPS surprise + 30-day estimate revisions5
Net-margin expansion (latest qtr vs year-ago qtr)10-2→0 · 0→0.4 · 3→1

Tags: Accelerating = EPS YoY growth rose in each of the last 3 quarters · Code 33 = EPS, sales growth and net margin all rose for 3 quarters · Turnaround = latest quarter profitable vs a year-ago loss · Big grower = EPS ≥ +40% and sales ≥ +20% · Estimates rising = FY consensus up >2% in 30 days · Limited data (see above).

Sources: SEC EDGAR XBRL companyfacts (primary); Massive financials; Yahoo Finance statements via yfinance (third-party, last resort). Q4 is derived as fiscal year minus 9-month YTD where not filed (marked “d”). Estimates: Yahoo Finance consensus via yfinance (third-party) (as-of dates on each card). Coverage today: 2268 names · 2001 full history · 2187 with consensus · 267 limited data. Config: research-tools/earnings_score_config.json.

ℹ️ How the overall score works

Overall (0–100) = 35% RS + 35% earnings + 15% sector bullishness + 15% peer momentum. RS and earnings carry most of the weight because Minervini’s leaders combine price leadership with earnings power; sector and peer momentum confirm the group is in play (most big winners come from leading groups) without letting a hot group carry a weak stock.

  • RS = 70% × IBD-style RS rating (percentile across the ranked universe) + 30% × RS rank within its SIC industry group (percentile).
  • Earnings = the earnings score; limited-data names get a neutral 45 (tagged) instead of zero.
  • Sector bullishness (SIC industry group with ≥ 8 ranked names, else the sector): share passing the Trend Template (30), share above the 50-day (20), median 1/3/6-month return percentile among groups (25), group median RS percentile (25).
  • Peer momentum: share of group members with RS 90+ (40), members in the RS Top 50 (20), actionable scanner breakouts (15), 4-week change in the share with RS 80+ (25). Leader = top 20% of its group by RS, laggard = bottom half.

A missing component is dropped and the other weights re-normalised; the report card shows a tag. Config: research-tools/composite_config.json.
